property_summary: For any call that succeeds, the return value must be true; the buggy version always returns true even when individual external calls fail, violating this invariant because the reference relies on transferFrom which may revert if the target contract does not implement it, while the bug uses transfer and silently succeeds with unused return data.
For any input where the callee address is a contract that does not implement transferFrom, the reference C reverts while the buggy M returns true.

For any input where the external call to caddress on transferFrom succeeds, the reference C should return true; the buggy M calls transfer instead, so if caddress returns false from transfer (e.g., via a contract that implements transfer and returns false), M returns true anyway, while the reference C reverts because transferFrom is not implemented or fails.

The transfer function must revert if any sub-call to transferFrom fails; the buggy version ignores call failures and always returns true, violating the invariant that a failed sub-call forces a revert.

For any call to transfer with equal-length arrays where at least one sub-call to an externally controlled transferFrom fails (reverts), the reference C must revert, while the buggy M ignores the failure and returns true.
No matter how many sub-calls succeed, if any sub-call to transferFrom reverts, C.transfer must revert; the mutant ignores the revert and returns true.
For any call to transfer with a callee that reverts on any transferFrom sub-call, the correct C must revert; the buggy M ignores the revert and returns true.
For any call to transfer with an adversarial callee that reverts on one transferFrom sub‑call, the reference C must revert, whereas the bug ignores that revert and returns true.
A transfer call with an empty _tos array must always revert, but the mutant allows it to succeed.
For any non-empty arrays _tos and v of equal length, transfer always returns true; the mutant removes the check allowing empty _tos, which changes behavior for empty arrays.
A call to transfer with identical arguments must either succeed or revert identically in both versions, but the mutant allows an empty _tos array to succeed instead of reverting.
For any input, transfer reverts if and only if _tos.length == 0; the buggy version allows _tos.length == 0 to succeed, violating the invariant that empty arrays always revert.
For any admissible input, a call to transfer that does not revert returns true; the mutant fails this because it can succeed where the reference reverts, which the assertion flags as a failure.

For every call to transfer, the low-level call to caddress must be made with the original 'from' parameter; the mutant uses msg.sender instead, causing a different source address for the ERC20 transferFrom when msg.sender != from.

For any input where msg.sender is not the same as the `from` parameter, the reference contract always succeeds (returns true), while the mutant contract succeeds only if msg.sender is the same as `from`.

The reference contract always succeeds when msg.sender is not the from address and the external call succeeds, but the mutant reverts because the ERC20 token will see msg.sender (the caller) instead of the approved from address.
